subject: BrightLabs pricing and packaging alignment
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Sam Park <sam.park@brightlabs.com>, Elena Ruiz <elena@brightlabs.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 30 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: BrightLabs pricing and packaging alignment

Hi Sam / Elena —

Great to meet yesterday. Per our conversation, I’m sending a compact proposal that maps the pricing bands BrightLabs talked about to a staged commitment model we can support. The attached "proposed_pricing_table.xlsx" shows: three usage tiers, a 12-month rate-match window for existing committed volume, and a separate bucket for low-latency KV-cache instances (important for your real-time inference workloads).

High-level asks from our side:
- Confirmation of your forecasted average qps and 95th percentile token rates for the first 12 months (we used your estimate 35M tokens/mo as a baseline).
- Agreement on a 6-month pilot with a one-time onboarding credit to offset migration costs.
- Permission to run a short perf benchmark on a representative workload before we finalize the KV-cache sizing.

We can consider a limited price-match to the incumbent for year one if BrightLabs commits to a staged ramp (details in the sheet). That match is conditional on a three-point compromise: explicit commit tiers, a short-term pilot credit, and mutual SLA definitions for latency and availability.

Next step: if you’re aligned, I’ll loop in Connor (Solutions) to size the KV cache and Markus (finance) to finalize the ramp tables and margin guardrails.

Thanks —
Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0128
Redwood Inference

Attachment: proposed_pricing_table.xlsx (spreadsheet, pricing bands and sample math)

From: Sam Park <sam.park@brightlabs.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Ruiz <elena@brightlabs.com>
Date: Thu, 30 Jul 2026 11:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: BrightLabs pricing and packaging alignment

Vanessa —

Thanks for sending this over. Quick notes from our side after reviewing the sheet with finance: we like the staged ramp but need stronger parity against our incumbent's effective blended rate for year one. Specifically:
- Can Redwood match the incumbent's blended per-token rate if we commit to the 12-month volume tier you outlined?
- The incumbent also provides a 90-day free pilot plus an implementation credit; can you stretch to match 90 days?
- We need assurances around KV-cache capacity — our latency tail matters here. Will you commit to a latency SLA for KV-backed calls (p95 under 80ms) or provide a fallback credit if we miss it?

We’d prefer to keep legal overhead light and use DocuSign for the amendment once pricing is finalized. I’ve copied Elena (CFO) for visibility — she’ll want to see the exact blended math and any one-time credits spelled out.

Sam Park
Head of Infrastructure | BrightLabs
sam.park@brightlabs.com

--

To: Sam Park <sam.park@brightlabs.com>, Elena Ruiz <elena@brightlabs.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 30 Jul 2026 13:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: BrightLabs pricing and packaging alignment

Sam / Elena —

Appreciate the clarity — short answers below and a proposed structure: please see the second tab of the attached pricing sheet for the net math.

1) Year-one rate-match: yes, we can provide an effective blended match for eligible committed volume for months 1–12, capped to the forecast band you sign. The caveat is we ask that BrightLabs agree to the staged ramp milestones (month 1 >= 40% baseline, month 6 >= 80%). If the ramp misses by more than two consecutive months, the match window converts to a smaller, time-limited credit rather than a permanent reprice.

2) Pilot duration/credits: we can extend to a 90-day pilot. Onboarding credit: we’ll provide a one-time SOW credit of up to $60k applied to your first invoice, tied to a 90-day pilot acceptance criteria.

3) KV-cache SLA: we can commit to a p95 latency target of 80ms for the KV-backed inference path under normal operational load, with an operational runbook. If we miss the SLA for two consecutive weeks, we’ll provide a service credit on the subsequent invoice (details in proposed addendum). We’ll need to validate on your representative load during the perf benchmark.

Internal note (cc Markus & Connor): margin sensitivity here — if we give the blended match + 90-day onboarding credit + KV credits we need an internal guardrail: limit the match to committed volumes up to the signed forecast + 15% overage. Markus, can finance confirm the minimum acceptable blended margin? Connor, can you confirm the perf benchmark window and what sample queries you need?

Assuming sign-off on those points we’ll produce an amendment with the pricing table and an SOW for the pilot; legal can add a simple addendum for the SLA credits and the 12-month match mechanics. Once you confirm, we’ll route via DocuSign.

Regards,
Vanessa Ortiz
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com

Attachment: proposed_pricing_table.xlsx (updated tab with match math)

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 31 Jul 2026 14:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: BrightLabs pricing and packaging alignment

Vanessa — forwarding my quick take after looking through the sheet:

- Finance can support the 12-month blended match but only if we hard cap the eligible volume (signed forecast + 15% as you suggested). Otherwise the tail risk kills the unit margin.
- The $60k onboarding credit is doable as a one-time contra, but we should split the exposure: $40k applied immediately, $20k held as a conditional credit after pilot acceptance. That reduces our effective immediate cash impact.
- SLA credits: keep them explicit and capped (e.g., max 5% of monthly invoice during the first 12 months).

Action items: Vanessa, please update the pricing sheet to include the cap and the split onboarding credit. Connor, confirm the perf benchmark spec so we can sign off on the SLA terms. I’ll draft a short addendum (redline-addendum.docx) for legal review and prepare the DocuSign envelope once we have the updated sheet.

-Markus
VP, Finance | Redwood Inference
markus_klein@redwood.com

- 48-hour representative trace (qps + token distribution + example prompt types)
- A list of 10 query classes that must hit p95 < 80ms on the KV path
- Access to a non-prod VPC endpoint or a sanitized replay (we can host the runner)

I confirm we can validate the SLA on that benchmark and provide a clear pass/fail acceptance which will trigger the $20k conditional credit release if passed. I’ll draft the perf spec and upload it to the shared Drive link (I’ll send the link in a follow-up).
